title: Phase 5 Operations Manual Package
description: Machine-testable operations manual for local mock platform handoff. It documents operator roles, local previews, allowlisted commands, review gates, generated evidence, and safety boundaries without enabling real providers, agents, MCP servers, cloud resources, sandboxes, or publish actions.

manualWorkflows.title: Daily local readiness check
expectedSignals: phase1 check returns success=true and data.passed=true.
delivery package reports missingRequired=0.
acceptance report reports acceptancePassed=true and safetyAssertionsPassed=true.

manualWorkflows.title: Content generation and review gate
expectedSignals: Generated Lab, Exam, Grading, and PPT DSL stay WAITING_REVIEW.
Candidate-facing exam previews do not reveal standard answers.
publishBlockedUntilApproved remains true.

manualWorkflows.title: High-risk MCP handoff review
expectedSignals: publish_lab and publish_exam only create review intent.
destroy_environment requires second confirmation and never destroys a real environment.
get_second_confirmation_status remains read-only.

manualWorkflows.title: Review real LLM PoC readiness gates
expectedSignals: Phase 5 mock baseline is frozen at 175/175.
Default provider remains mock.
Real LLM PoC is limited to explicit opt-in Lab DSL generation.
Provider runtime guard keeps timeout/retry/concurrency/redaction/schema/review gates enabled and real calls disabled.
Real LLM PoC adapter remains disabled after runtime guard and preflight checks.
Real LLM dry-run plan passes locally without checking secret presence or creating tasks.
Real LLM approval gate can mark implementation task ready without authorizing a real call.
Real Provider SDK PoC harness requires the SDK task blueprint and still stops at opt-in or disabled-provider gates without importing SDKs, checking secrets, opening network, or creating tasks.
Real SDK enablement switch design may be ready for a future implementation task but still does not authorize real calls.

Real SDK minimal implementation shell requires enablement and explicit implementation opt-in, then still stops at the implementation-disabled gate without importing SDKs, checking secrets, opening network, or creating tasks.
Real SDK dependency and environment gate can mark a future dependency task ready but still does not install SDKs, import SDKs, check secret presence, or call network.

Real SDK dependency install plan can mark a future install implementation review ready but still does not generate install commands, install SDKs, resolve package metadata, modify lockfiles, check secret presence, or call network.

Real SDK dependency installer audit can mark a future disabled installer implementation task ready but still does not materialize commands, install SDKs, resolve packages, modify files, check secret presence, or call network.

Real SDK dependency change preview can mark a future dependency change implementation task ready but still does not write files, generate diffs, install SDKs, resolve package metadata, check secret presence, or call network.

Real SDK dependency patch proposal can mark a future patch implementation task ready but still does not write patch files, apply patches, write dependency files, generate diff artifacts, resolve package metadata, check secret presence, or call network.

Real SDK dependency readonly diff review can mark a future readonly diff review ready but still does not read live dependency files, write diff artifacts, generate patches, resolve package metadata, modify dependency files, check secret presence, or call network.

Real SDK dependency final execution confirmation can mark a future reviewed dependency execution task ready but still does not grant execution approval, create tasks, mutate dependency files, execute commands, install dependencies, check secrets, call network, or call real LLMs.

Real SDK dependency execution task creation can mark a local disabled task creation model ready but still does not persist tasks, queue work, dispatch execution, mutate dependency files, execute commands, install dependencies, check secrets, call network, or call real LLMs.
